subject: Residency exception request: split-tunnel CMK process for private deployment

Subject: Residency exception and key custody approach for private deploy

Hi Laura,

Thanks for the demo last week. Our security team has a follow-up around a corner case: MedAtlas needs a documented procedure to allow transient US processing for a customer-hosted private deployment while the master CMK remains under our control. The ask is narrow — a temporary exception window during onboarding and certain maintenance tasks — and must include:

- An auditable sign-off flow for each exception
- Clear operator access boundaries and telemetry captured
- Proof that no customer plaintext is persisted outside the VPC after the window

We heard the term 'split-tunnel CMK' in the demo (where a small shard can be held by Redwood to enable runtime operations). Can you share a concise process we can present to our legal and infosec teams? I attached the residency-exception-form our legal team uses.

Sara
Sara King
Head of Security Operations, MedAtlas

Subject: Re: Residency exception and key custody approach for private deploy

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear list.

High-level: we support a controlled, auditable residency-exception workflow for Private deployments. The pattern we recommend is a two-step "split-tunnel CMK" arrangement where:

1) Customer retains the CMK master material (KMS/ HSM that they control).
2) Redwood holds an ephemeral operational shard (a limited key share) inside a hardened HSM in the customer's VPC for the minimal window required.

Key controls we propose to include in the formal process:
- Explicit written approval from the named MedAtlas approver (your form works).
- Timeboxed exception (default 72 hours, extendable with re-approval).
- Breakglass justification, ticket ID, and bind to the exception request.
- Operator actions gated to named Redwood engineers with recorded sessions and telemetry forwarded to MedAtlas SIEM.
- Post-window automated key zeroization and attestation signed by Redwood.

I'll draft a one-page process + an operator checklist and share. Looping in Irene (privacy) and Karthik (ops) to confirm telemetry and the technical lock-step.

– Laura
Laura Bennett
Principal, Security & Privacy 
Redwood Inference

Sara / Laura — brief technical clarifications from privacy and compliance: 

- We cannot hold any long-term key material outside your control. Any Redwood shard must be ephemeral and derivable only for the exception window.
- The shard design must cryptographically ensure that neither party alone can decrypt historical ciphertext — i.e., require co-signer or threshold operation.
- Telemetry: we will produce a signed attestation bundle post-event (timestamped key operations, operator identity, and actions performed). We recommend including a non-repudiable log stream to your SIEM.

I'll attach a diagram of the split-tunnel concept (minimalist: split-tunnel-cmk-diagram.png) and a proposed audit field set for your form.

Irene Choi
Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is very helpful. A few procurement/legal asks before we proceed: 

1) Contract language: need a short clause for our DPA that the exception is timeboxed, auditable, and that Redwood will return a signed attestation within 5 business days after zeroization.
2) Subprocessors: will there be any third-party (e.g., HSM vendor) access during the window? If so, they must be listed as subprocessors with limited scope.
3) Evidence: standard evidence package is (a) operator session recording, (b) signed attestation, (c) proof of zeroization (hash of destroyed keys + timestamp).

If you can provide the draft clause and confirm subprocessors we can proceed to a procurement review.

Sara
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: procurement@medatlas.com
Date: 2026-06-02T09:16:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Residency exception and key custody approach for private deploy

Sara — quick operational notes and subprocessor callout: 

- HSM vendor: Redwood will use a customer-provisioned HSM cluster in the VPC when available (preferred). If the customer cannot provide HSM hardware, Redwood can deploy a validated HSM image running in the customer's cloud tenancy; that image uses Redwood-managed modules but we will declare the cloud HSM provider as a subprocessors list entry (e.g., AWS CloudHSM or Azure Dedicated HSM) limited strictly to the exception instance.
- Subprocessor access: no third-party employees will access plaintext; Redwood staff access is controlled via time-limited operator accounts and recorded sessions.
- Draft DPA clause (text below) — feel free to pull into your form: 

"During an approved residency exception window, Redwood may deploy a time-limited operational key share (\"Operational Shard\") to enable required on-premise or VPC maintenance. The Operational Shard is ephemeral, cryptographically insufficient alone to decrypt customer data, and will be destroyed at the end of the approved window. Redwood will provide Customer with a signed attestation and evidence package within five (5) business days of shard destruction. Any third-party providers engaged to host HSM functionality for the exception will be listed as subprocessors with access strictly limited to the exception scope."

I'll coordinate with Ops to ensure the zeroization proof format is the SHA256 of the destroyed shard material wrapped in a signed attestation.

—Karthik
Director, Platform Operations, Redwood Inference
